$comment: GNU `__attribute__((aligned(N)))` ON A TYPEDEF is ACCEPTED and **CONFERRED** (cycle P66, lane `al`). The alias's alignment must reach three places and the exit code gates all three, so a partial fix cannot read as a complete one: (1) `_Alignof(A8) == 8` and `sizeof(A8) == 4`; (2) an OBJECT of the alias type placed on 8 in static storage AND in a frame slot; (3) a STRUCT MEMBER of that type placed on 8, which is what makes `struct S { char c; A8 v; }` sizeof 16 rather than 8. exit = 42; 7 / 8 / 9 name which observation failed. ★★ THE REFERENCES CONFER IT, THEY DO NOT MERELY TOLERATE IT. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-09, each reference probed SEPARATELY on its own translation unit, rc read DIRECTLY and never through a pipeline: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 each compile `typedef int __attribute__((aligned(8))) A8;` rc 0 with ZERO bytes on stderr at -Wall -Wextra, `_Static_assert(_Alignof(A8) == 8)` PASSING and the `== 4` twin FAILING, in BOTH orders (attribute after the specifiers and before them); an EXECUTED binary returns 42 from THIS FILE at -O0 and -O2 on both; mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 agrees on every arm it was given; aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc accepts the layout claims. ★ MSVC 19.51.36257 ABSTAINS ON THE SPELLING ONLY — it has no `__attribute__` syntax at all (C2143) — and its vote on the CONSTRUCT is cast through the spelling it implements and is the SAME vote: `typedef __declspec(align(8)) int A8;` compiles rc 0 with `int p[(__alignof(A8)==8)?1:-1]` while the `==4` twin fails C2118. So an over-aligned type ALIAS is conferred by ALL THREE references, not two; an abstention on a surface spelling is recorded AS an abstention and never as agreement. DSS was BELOW the union here, refusing a program every reference compiles, in the SDK-dominant spelling. ★ SIZE IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED AND THAT IS MEASURED: `sizeof(A8)` stays 4 while `_Alignof(A8)` is 8, and BOTH references consequently REFUSE an ARRAY of the alias ('alignment of array elements is greater than element size' / 'isn't a multiple of its alignment'), so no array of A8 appears in this file and a fix that rounded size up to alignment would accept a program no reference accepts. ★★ IT IS THE OPPOSITE ANSWER FROM THE ISO SPELLING AND BOTH ARE RIGHT: `typedef _Alignas(8) int A8;` is REFUSED by gcc, clang AND MSVC (C7704) and by ISO C 6.7.6p2, so DSS refuses it too — [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS-TYPEDEF-PARAM-PARSE]] (P58), RE-MEASURED this cycle and still holding. One construct, two spellings, opposite verdicts; a fix keyed on the CONTEXT would have admitted both and put DSS ABOVE the union in the same stroke it fixed being below it. ★ THE REFERENCE ORACLE FOR THIS FILE IS gcc AND clang AND IT WAS RUN, NOT ASSUMED: `gcc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra` and `clang -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra` at -O0 and -O2 all BUILD it with stderr EMPTY and the binary EXITS 42 — an example only DSS accepts is not a witness, it is a second copy of the bug. RED-ON-DISABLE, and the two halves are DIFFERENT questions that must red DIFFERENT pins: ACCEPTANCE — restore the typedef sink's refusal in `semantic_analyzer.cpp` and this file does not COMPILE at all (error[S_AlignasInvalidContext]) and stops exiting 42; CONFERRAL — drop the alignment before layout (e.g. key the layout memo by `stripVolatile` again instead of `layoutRoot`) and the file still COMPILES and returns 7, 8 or 9, naming which of the three observations failed. That second direction is the silent-wrong-answer one, and it is why this file is a RUNNABLE witness rather than a parse pin. Data-model-independent; one exit code across all four targets including the shipped release pipeline.
